costNote: Building the machines that build chips. Gross margin hit 50.3% — the 13th straight quarter of year-over-year expansion — because the mix keeps shifting to higher-value systems.

opex.name: Research, development & engineering
opex.note: The EPIC Center program now counts 11 partnership engagements with leading chipmakers and universities — co-developing the next process nodes.

opex.name: Marketing & selling
opex.note: Selling and supporting systems at the world's largest fabs.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Down from $204M a year ago — corporate costs were cut and reallocated to the segments this year.

otherDetail.label: Interest & other, net
otherDetail.note: A net expense this quarter as mark-to-market losses on strategic equity investments outweighed interest income (a year ago this line added $396M).

segments.name: Semiconductor Systems
segments.note: The wafer-fab equipment itself — foundry/logic 67% of segment sales, DRAM 26%, flash 7%. Segment operating margin 37.7%; management raised its calendar-2026 outlook for this segment again.

segments.name: Applied Global Services
segments.note: Spares, service and fab-optimization subscriptions — the recurring layer. Operating margin 30.1%.

segments.name: Display & other
segments.note: Display equipment and corporate/other items — the small remainder.

sources.label: Applied Materials Q3 FY2026 earnings release — SEC EDGAR Ex-99.1 (8-K, Aug 13, 2026)

takeaways.text: Record revenue, up 25%, with the highest sequential growth in company history — AI chip demand for leading-edge logic, DRAM and advanced packaging is pulling equipment orders.
takeaways.title: AI capex, monetized

takeaways.text: Gross margin expanded for the 13th consecutive quarter year over year — Applied keeps capturing more value per tool as chips get harder to make.
takeaways.title: Margins keep climbing

takeaways.text: The tax bill was unusually light (12.7% of pre-tax income vs 30.6% a year ago), flattering GAAP EPS growth of 43%. Operating performance alone was still a record.
takeaways.title: A tax tailwind too

verdict: The AI build-out's arms dealer: record $9.1B revenue, record operating income, and demand visibility into 2027.
